title: Six Potential Replacements for USMNT Boss Mauricio Pochettino Following Man Utd Exit
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely4:00 PM ESTMauricio Pochettino could be on his way out. /  Omar Vega/Getty ImagesU.S. men’s national team manager Mauricio Pochettino is headed for the exit door, inking a deal on Friday to take charge of Manchester United, a reported two-and-a-half year tenure at Old Trafford that will officially begin on Wednesday. He replaces Michael Carrick, who was axed only 24 hours prior after commanding the the Red Devils to just one Premier League win across the first 10 matches of the new season.

Pochettino’s exit comes as a sudden and major blow to the USMNT, who is currently grouped for the November international window. Rumors of United’s interest in Pochettino only began to surface on Monday, and the 54-year-old Argentine boss also just signed a four-year contract renewal with U.S. Soccer in August, which retained him through the 2030 World Cup.

While Pochettino has agreed to see out the USMNT’s two-legged series against Haiti for the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals over the next few days, U.S. Soccer has much work to do to find his long-term replacement.

The U-23 USMNT manager, Steve Cherundolo, will command the USMNT for the December friendly against Jamaica, and competitive fixtures don’t return until March, giving the federation a little bit of breathing room to make the right decision.
It also has at least an extra $10 million to play with, thanks to the buyout fee United was forced to cough up for Pochettino’s hand.

Due to the strong foundation Pochettino has laid in the States, the Americans have big ambitions for the 2030 World Cup. They’ll need a leader that cannot just sustain the work the Argentine has done, but actually advance it.
Here are six viable candidates that could fill his big shoes.

B.J. Callaghan led Nashville SC to the best regular season in MLS history. / Jeff Dean/MLS/Getty ImagesOff the back of making Major League Soccer history, B.J. Callaghan could be an outside contender to replace Pochettino.
Callaghan extended his contract with Nashville SC through the 2028–29 season in February; however, U.S. Soccer may still be inclined to pry him away.

Not only does the 45-year-old out of Ventnor City, N.J. have experience with the USMNT—serving as the team’s interim manager back in 2023, he has also proven his managerial worth tenfold over the past two seasons in MLS.

2025 was his first full season in Nashville, and although the club did not win the MLS Cup that year, Callaghan still achieved several club records, including the most single-season wins (22 all competition) and the longest unbeaten streak (15 all competitions). He also led the Boys in Gold to their first-ever trophy: the Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup.

His 2026 campaign has been even more prolific, establishing this Nashville squad as the single greatest regular season team in MLS history. They surpassed Inter Miami’s 2024 squad (74) for the highest points tally in MLS regular season history (77) and also set league records for most wins (23), fewest losses (3), points per game (2.26), win percentage (79.4), fewest goals conceded (25) and the largest Supporters’ Shield points margin (13).
It was total domination from Callaghan’s men, who seem destined to hoist their first-ever MLS Cup. Meanwhile, their manager could be headed out the door.
Pellegrino Matarazzo has found great success in Europe. /  Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty ImagesPellegrino Matarazzo is another American that could be a strong successor to Pochettino.
The 48-year-old out of Wayne, N.J. and graduate of Columbia University’s soccer program is now at the helm of Real Sociedad in the Spanish La Liga, where he has made quite a name for himself.

He touched down in San Sebastián in December 2025, replacing the fired Sergio Francisco. Matarazzo, who became the first American manager in La Liga, inherited a dismal team sitting 15th in La Liga, just one point above the relegation zone.

The American boss completely rebuilt La Real, and by April, they were hoisting the Copa del Rey title after a dramatic penalty shootout against Atlético Madrid. He set even more history in the process, becoming the first American manager to win a major trophy in one of Europe’s top five leagues. The team finished the 2026–7 season in a much-improved 10th place.
The club has been off to a strong start to the new season as well, currently sitting fifth in league standings.

Whether or not Matarazzo, who recently signed a two-year contract extension with the club, would want to depart Real Sociedad less than a year into his tenure remains to be seen; however, he has openly expressed interest in the USMNT position in the past.
